rules.statement: A married woman's immovable property becomes her separate estate, but she has only a prima facie right to the rents of that property, and the husband may step in whenever he pleases and claim it as his own under section 19.
rules.supporting_quote: "Section 9 clearly provides, by necessary implication, that not only the immovable property with which it deals but the rents of that property become the married woman's separate estate. The object of the section was, in my opinion, to confer on married women the kind of interest in property which the Courts of Equity in England, and subsequently the Married Women's Property Act, 1870, recognized."
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: Section 9 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, 1876 (No. 15 of 1876)
